chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani informed me, saying: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) gave a sermon to the people on the Day of Fitr, saying: O people! Indeed this day of yours is a day in which the righteous are rewarded and the wrongdoers suffer loss. It is the day most resembling the Day of your Resurrection. So remember, through your going out from your homes to your place of prayer, your coming out from your graves to your Lord. And remember, through your standing in your place of prayer, your standing before your Lord. And remember, through your return to your homes, your return to your abodes in Paradise or the Fire.

And know, O servants of God, that the least reward for fasting men and women is that an angel calls to them on the last day of the month of Ramadan: 'Rejoice, O servants of God, for your past sins have been forgiven. So look to how you will conduct yourselves henceforth.'

key_terms.الأجداث: Graves (ajdath), a Quranic term for burial places
key_terms.الفطر: Eid al-Fitr, the festival marking the end of Ramadan fasting
key_terms.تستأنفون: You resume/begin anew, referring to post-Ramadan conduct
key_terms.قيامتكم: Your resurrection (qiyama), the Day of Judgment
key_terms.مصلاكم: Your place of prayer (musalla), the open-air Eid prayer grounds

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Day of Eid al-Fitr and its resemblance to the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In this sermon delivered on Eid al-Fitr, Imam Ali (AS) draws powerful parallels between the Eid prayer rituals and the Day of Resurrection. He reminds the congregation in Kufa that leaving their homes for prayer mirrors emerging from graves, standing in prayer mirrors standing before God, and returning home mirrors returning to eternal abodes in Paradise or Hell. He concludes by declaring that the minimum reward for those who fasted Ramadan is angelic assurance of forgiveness, with an admonition to maintain righteous conduct going forward.
